interface:
For the type set $\mathcal G$ and cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], define $\Gamma\approx_0\Gamma'$ when $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')=F(\Gamma',\Gamma)=0$. Form the quotient monoid of types under this relation, with product induced by type composition and positive scaling induced by $t\Gamma$. Define formal differences to be pairs $(A,B)$ of quotient types, with

$$(A,B)\equiv(A',B')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists C\text{ such that }A\times B'\times C\approx_0 A'\times B\times C.$$

The set $V_F$ is the set of these pair classes. Define addition by $(A,B)+(D,E)=(A\times D,B\times E)$, negation by $-(A,B)=(B,A)$, and positive scaling by $t(A,B)=(tA,tB)$. Set zero to the class of $(1,1)$, where $1$ is the empty unit type. The representative-independence and real-vector-space laws are proved in [[lem-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space-well-defined]].

interface:
Let $I$ be a set of tagged simple-system labels. For each $i\in I$, let $n_i\ge1$ and let $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$ be nonempty, open, and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$, $u\in\mathbb R$, $v\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$. A state is a tagged pair $(i,x)$; distinct labels remain distinct even when their coordinate tuples agree. Positive scaled copies and finite compounds use the coefficient maps and total coefficient mass of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only for equal-mass compounds. For a tagged state $x$, $e_x$ denotes the unit point mass at that state; the zero compound is the empty map. Write $A\sim B$ when both $A\prec B$ and $B\prec A$, and write $A\prec\prec B$ when $A\prec B$ but $B\not\prec A$.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $te_x$ is equivalent to $se_x+(t-s)e_x$ for every state label $x$, $t>0$, and $0<s<t$; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:(i,x)\prec(i,y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $0<t<1$, the compound $((i,tx),(i,(1-t)y))$ compares to $(i,tx+(1-t)y)$; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with finite slope $P_i(x)$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

interface: Let $u,v$ be finite-support real coefficient maps on the tagged state labels of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] with equal total coefficient. For a tagged state $x$, the unit point mass $e_x$ is as defined in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Put $d=v-u$, $d^+(x)=\max(d(x),0)$ and $d^-(x)=\max(-d(x),0)$. Define $u\preceq_s v$ to mean $d^-\prec d^+$ under the compound relation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Write $u\sim_s v$ when both $u\preceq_s v$ and $v\preceq_s u$. These are formal signed comparison maps, not physical negative amounts. The positive and negative parts are finite-support compounds of equal mass. The ordinary-order compatibility and signed-order laws follow from [[lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellation]]. If $u\sim_s v$, then $cu\sim_s cv$ for every real $c$: positive $c$ uses scaling, $c=0$ is reflexivity, and negative $c$ swaps the positive and negative parts while equivalence supplies both comparison directions.

interface:
For two simple domains $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$ and $\Gamma_j\subset\mathbb R^{n_j+1}$, write their coordinates $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$. Their thermal-join domain is

$$\Delta_{ij}:=\{(u,v_i,v_j):\exists u_i,u_j,\ (u_i,v_i)\in\Gamma_i,\ (u_j,v_j)\in\Gamma_j,\ u=u_i+u_j\}.$$

Write $J_{ij}(x,y)$ for the join state with the summed energy coordinate and the unchanged work coordinates. A compound pair $(x,y)$ and $J_{ij}(x,y)$ have the same total energy and work coordinates but are distinct tagged objects. Define $x\sim_T y$ exactly when the compound pair and its join state are accessible in both directions. Nested joins use the declared reassociation and permutation identifications.

Assume every finite join is itself a simple domain satisfying [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. The contact hypotheses are mathematical assumptions on the common relation: (T1) $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$; (T2) every join state has at least one reversible split into component states at its stated coordinates, and the equal-state split of any state into positive scaled copies of itself is reversible; (T3) $\sim_T$ is transitive; (T4) for every simple state $x$ there are states $x_0,x_1$ in its domain with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$; (T5) for every ordered pair of simple systems, every $x$ in the first and every work coordinate $v$ in the second's projection $\rho(\Gamma_j):=\{v:\exists u,(u,v)\in\Gamma_j\}$, there is a state $y$ with work coordinate $v$ and $x\sim_T y$.

For the completed calibrator branch, add (C1) **join coherence**: whenever $x\sim_T y$, the join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ is thermally equivalent to each of $x$ and $y$ under the nested-join identifications. The coordinate sum in the definition alone does not assert C1. In later theorem statements, T1–T5 and C1 are explicitly listed as hypotheses; they are not treated as established physical laws.

This relation is well-defined, agrees with $\prec$ on nonnegative maps, is invariant under adding a common signed map, is transitive, and is closed under addition of two comparisons. No comparison hypothesis is used.

interface: Let $C$ be a nonempty convex set in a finite-dimensional affine Euclidean space $H$ of dimension $k\ge1$, let $\operatorname{aff}C=H$, and put $K=\overline{C}^{\,H}$. If $z\in\partial_H K$ (that is, $z\in K$ and every relative neighborhood of $z$ meets $H\setminus K$), then there is a nonzero linear functional $\ell$ on the translation space of $H$ such that $\ell(q-z)\le0$ for all $q\in C$. If $C\subset\mathbb R^d$ has affine dimension at most $d-2$, then every $z\in C$ has at least two distinct ambient supporting hyperplanes containing $\operatorname{aff}C$.

interface:
Let $I$ be a nonempty set of primitive simple-system labels containing a distinguished meter label $m$. Assume every finite separated product is explicitly represented by its finitely many tagged elementary factors; positive scaling and finite product are the only identifications. Suppose the join-closed family satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]], and fix a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then one can choose, for every $i\in I$, an additive constant and positive scale for its same-type entropy so that

$$S\big((t_1i_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_ni_n,x_n)\big)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$$

is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison on every finite separated product. No conclusion is asserted for transitions that change composition.

interface:
Under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], each simple domain has one orientation sign $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$, constant across the domain, such that at fixed work coordinate $v$, $x\prec y$ exactly when $\varepsilon_i(u_y-u_x)\ge0$. In coordinates oriented so $\varepsilon_i=1$, for each $x\in\Gamma_i$ the projection $\rho_x$ of $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$ onto work coordinates is open and connected; the boundary is the graph $(u_x(v),v)$ of a $C^1$ function with locally Lipschitz derivative

$$Du_x(v)=-P_i(u_x(v),v).$$

If $y\in\partial A_x$, then $A_y=A_x$ and their boundary graphs agree.
